summary: SSE streaming silent pause (~25-40s) during GPU memory compaction on Dedicated worker causing mid-generation stall
description: Issue summary: Customers using dedicated capacity reported SSE/chat streams silently pausing mid-generation for ~25-40s then resuming. Impact: Interactive chat UX times out or appears frozen for users; some clients hit SDK timeouts and close the socket, resulting in truncated replies. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) in us-east; affects a subset of workers on machines with >48GB GPU memory running quantized models. First reported by BrightGuide Analytics during peak usage window. Observed behavior: Server keeps producing keep-alive events but no token chunks are emitted for the pause window. When generation resumes, multiple tokens are emitted in a burst to catch up.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision dedicated instance with gpt-redi-6B-quantized-v2 pinned in us-east
2) Start an SSE chat stream with long-generation prompt (expected >600 tokens) and response_continuation enabled
3) Simulate sustained load (50 concurrent chats) to force normal batching and occasional KV checkpointing
4) Observe that ~10-15% of streams experience a silent pause ~25-40s into generation; server keep-alives continue but data tokens stop
5) Remove/disable the scheduled memory compaction task on the worker and repeat — pause frequency drops to ~0%
logs: [2026-03-12T15:08:04Z] worker-71 WARN memory-compactor triggered: active_allocations=0.92 total_free=3.1GB
[2026-03-12T15:08:04Z] worker-71 DEBUG cuda-defrag blocking on stream 3 for 26080ms
[2026-03-12T15:08:04Z] http-sse connection keepalive sent to client_id=bg-conn-9
[2026-03-12T15:08:30Z] worker-71 INFO cuda-defrag completed; generation resumed; tokens_emitted=+320
investigation: SRE initial triage correlated stalls with the on-host memory compaction/defragmentation routine that runs as part of periodic KV checkpointing and a background 'memory-compactor' service. NVML traces show a spike in pci mem operations and a blocking CUDA stream wait for ~25-40s at the same timestamps as customer reports. pprof of the runtime during an incident shows the generation coroutine is blocked waiting on a GPU defrag mutex while the SSE connection remains open and keepalive frames continue. Pattern reproduced reliably on dedicated workers with >40GB allocations and when a background snapshot/compaction coincides with long in-flight generations. The compaction is synchronous and uses a single-threaded CUDA stream which starves generation kernels. We confirmed disabling the compaction on a single host removed the pauses. No changes to the customer SDK or networking path were found. Related PR introduces an async compaction path: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1426
comments: 2026-03-12 16:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Received initial report from BrightGuide. Customer says the UI freezes for ~30s and then resumes with a long chunk of text. They hit client-side 45s timeout in some flows.

2026-03-12 17:12 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Captured NVML traces and pprof from worker-71. Evidence points at synchronous memory compaction (cuda-defrag) blocking generation streams. Reproduced locally by enabling compactor on a dev dedicated node.
2026-03-13 09:03 - BrightGuide Support (Customer): We can reproduce on our end; disabling the 'auto-continue' option reduces impact but is not acceptable. Please advise ETA for fix.

2026-03-13 13:45 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Deployed a temporary mitigation — compactor disabled on pool us-east-dedicated-large between 13:30-14:30. Customer reports 0 incidents in that window. Working on non-blocking compaction patch.

2026-03-14 08:20 - Product Ops (K. Nguyen): Scheduling follow-up to audit compaction schedule and add metric alert on cuda-defrag blocking >10s. Action owner: infra-team; ETA for rollout of async compaction: 2026-03-21.
resolution: Workaround: Disabled synchronous memory compaction on impacted dedicated pools and adjusted KV checkpoint timing to off-peak windows (00:00-03:00 UTC) to avoid coinciding with customer peak. Patch: Merged non-blocking compaction PR implementing GPU-friendly defrag on a separate CUDA stream (PR 1426). Planned rollout: staggered canary to 10% of dedicated hosts on 2026-03-20, full rollout targeted 2026-03-21 after monitoring. Follow-ups: add alert for >5s CUDA stream blocking, add dashboard tile for compaction events, and update runbook to include immediate mitigation steps. Customer notified and opted into canary.
